flags.last_choice_ch1_mary_ellen: Vessel calling North Point, say again your name. Over.
flags.last_choice_ch1_radio_check: I know what night it is, Morag.
flags.last_choice_ch1_rory_call: Stay where you are, Rory. I'll find you. Over.
flags.last_choice_ch1_rory_in: Your grandfather said a lot of things, Rory.
flags.last_choice_ch2_gannet: Confirm your position and I'll talk you through the West Gut. Over.
flags.last_choice_ch2_mary_ellen: Who is this? Identify yourself. Over.
flags.last_choice_ch2_trace: I was there. I was twenty-three.
flags.last_choice_ch3_elspeth: I'm sorry, Miss Ross. I was there that night.
flags.last_choice_ch3_notes_b: The log says oh-two-ten. The log is right.

history.text: Sixteen-twenty. The sun's gone behind Pabbay and taken the colour with it.
Dark as a press up here. The cells are flat again. The engineer's been saying since Easter they're tired.
Sunday the fourteenth of November. I wrote the date at the top of the page this morning and sat looking at it.
Twenty-one winters on the lights, and the wind still sounds like someone trying the door.
The phone's been dead since the September gale. The radio's all the company there is till Thursday.
The torch first, top shelf by the door. Then the engine, and the lights. Then lighting-up time, and the long quiet.
She catches on the second turn and settles into that low knock you feel through your boots.
The lamps come up. That's better.
Fourteen amps and climbing. She'll come up.
Mind the temperature. That engine was old when Father was keeper.
Now, lighting-up time. The console, under the east window.
[A carrier on Channel 16. Two clicks. No voice.]
Somebody keyed a set on sixteen. Twice. Nobody spoke.
Some boy with his father's handset. On the Sabbath. His mother'll skelp him.
The motor takes up the optic overhead. Twelve turns a minute, same as the day they fitted it.
Normal power. Forty miles on a clear night. Tonight won't be clear.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, North Point, this is Stornoway Coastguard, Stornoway Coastguard. Evening radio check, over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stornoway, North Point. Reading you loud and clear, over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Loud and clear also. Anything to report? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Light exhibited at sixteen-forty. Engine running, batteries on charge. Nothing on the radar. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Roger. Gale warning for Hebrides and Minches. South-westerly seven, rising severe gale nine before dawn. Visibility poor in rain. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Received. Gale nine before dawn. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: And Callum. It's the fourteenth.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I know what night it is, Morag.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. I thought you might. I'll be on till six. Shout if you want company on the set. Stornoway out.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: North Point Light, North Point Light, this is the Kittiwake, Kittiwake, eh, Sierra Yankee three-seven. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Kittiwake, North Point. Go ahead, over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Callum, is that you? Thank God. Sorry, eh, North Point. I'm coming in from the Flannans, and the rain's that thick I can't see my own bow. I was meant to pick up the Sound an hour ago. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: And, eh. Don't be telling my mother I was out on the Sabbath. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: I've stopped her. I'm just sitting here like a gull on a fence post. Can you put me in? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stay where you are, Rory. I'll find you. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Holding. Holding. Right. I'm holding. Over.
First I need to know where he is. The radio at the desk. Ask him to confirm his position.
Bearing and range from the light. On the radar he's that echo north of the reef, a little east of the dashed line.
The North Sound runs straight in on oh-oh-oh. Bring his head round thirty degrees at a time until he's pointing down the line.
Once he can see the light and he's on the line, he'll find the channel buoys himself.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: North Point, Kittiwake! I've got the green on the Sound. I've got it! Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Keep it fine on your starboard bow and come in slow. North Point. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: Aye. Aye, I see it. Here, Callum, you'll laugh, but my grandfather used to say there's a boat out in the East Gut on nights like this. No lights. Just waiting. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Your grandfather said a lot of things, Rory.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: He did. He did. Half of them were true, mind. Over.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: I'm in the Sound now. Thanks, North Point. I'll stand you a dram at Christmas. Kittiwake out.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Are you awake over there? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Stornoway, North Point. Wide awake. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Good. The set's quiet and the kettle's broken. Talk to me. Off the log, Callum.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: What's on your mind, Morag?

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Donald's birthday would have been Thursday. Nine years. You'd think it would get easier, wouldn't you.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: It doesn't get easier. You just get stronger arms.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. That's about it. Your father used to say that. About the lamp-room weights.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Is it true what they say in Tarbert? Twenty-one years and you've never once missed lighting-up?

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Never once.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Like father, like son. He kept that station like a kirk, so they say.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Stornoway listening on sixteen. Out.
Eighteen-thirty, radio check, gale warning. Ten to seven, Kittiwake in by the North Sound. Twenty-three-twenty-five, Stornoway on sixteen. All well.
The same small square letters I learned at the school in Tarbert. Father always said I wrote like a clerk.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...North Point... North Point... this is... Mary Ellen... Mary Ellen...

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...we cannot see your light... repeat... we cannot see your light...

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Vessel calling North Point, say again your name. Over.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...Mary... Ellen...
Static. Then nothing. Not even the carrier.
The light is burning. I can hear the motor through the ceiling.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Callum. Did you hear that? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I heard it.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Mary Ellen. Somebody's idea of a joke. On this night. I'll find out who. Stornoway out.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Go ahead, Morag.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: I've rung round. Nobody's reporting a Mary Ellen. The register's had nothing by that name since nineteen fifty-three. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Lost with seven of the eight aboard, the skipper among them. Presumed. You know all this.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I know it.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Aye. You would.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Callum. You were on the light that night. With your father.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I was there. I was twenty-three.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: I know. I took the call. I was twenty-six and it was my first winter on the set.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Watch your radar. If somebody's out there playing silly beggars, they're close. That signal was strong. Stornoway out.
There. An echo. Bearing oh-four-six, a hundred yards off the East Gut rocks.
Not moving. Not fading with the sweep the way sea clutter does.
...And now it's gone. Sea clutter. It has to be sea clutter.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: North Point, this is the schooner Gannet. Hector Macleod. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Gannet, North Point. Go ahead, Hector.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: I've two passengers sick as dogs and no stars to steer by. I'm somewhere west of you, I think. I'd take a bearing kindly. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Confirm your position and I'll talk you through the West Gut. Over.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Right you are. I'm in your hands, North Point. Over.
West Gut, three-one-four. Line her up on the dashed line and she'll do the rest.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Gannet's in the Gut and the passengers have stopped praying. Grand job, North Point. Over.

history.name: Hector Macleod
history.speaker: HECTOR
history.text: Here. Tell your father I was asking for him. Oh. Och, I'm sorry, Callum. Thirteen years and I still forget. Gannet out.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...Lighthouse... lighthouse... is Iain Mackay on watch?

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...tell Iain... we cannot... see the light...

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Who is this? Identify yourself. Over.

history.name: Mary Ellen
history.speaker: MARY ELLEN
history.text: ...he knows who...
Nothing. Carrier gone.
"Tell Iain." Nobody's called him Iain in this room since the funeral.
The old logs are in the box on the storage shelf. Nineteen fifty-three. Fifteenth of November.
I know what it says. I don't need to open it.
I open it.
Fifteenth November, nineteen fifty-three. Oh-two-ten. "Light extinguished approx. two minutes, mantle failure. Relit oh-two-twelve."
"Trawler observed standing in too close at oh-one-thirty. No response to light." Signed, I. Mackay, P.K.
Small square letters. A clerk's hand. Tonight's page is lying open on the desk.
Eighteen years, and my hand hasn't changed at all.
[A grinding shudder overhead. The optic stops.]
The motor's labouring. Amber lamp on the console. The beam's stuck.
Motor off before she takes the main with her. Then free it by hand, the way the note says.
[A clunk you feel in your teeth]
Free again.
The bearing repeater says oh-four-six. The East Gut.
Father's note on the console, and my lines under his. "Free by hand." Forty-nine. December fifty-three. Sixty-one.
December fifty-three. Three weeks after. As if writing it down would count for something.
It always sticks at forty-six.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: All stations, all stations, this is Stornoway Coastguard. Gale warning. Hebrides, Minches: south-westerly severe gale nine, increasing storm ten, imminent. Visibility very poor. Stornoway out.
Ten. The windows are already shivering in their frames.

history.name: Corrie May
history.speaker: CORRIE
history.text: North Point, Corrie May. Coming in from the east, and the sea's gone mad. I've lost the shore lights altogether. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Corrie May, North Point. I'll put you in the East Gut. Confirm your position when I call. Over.

history.name: Lowestoft Star
history.speaker: LOWESTOFT
history.text: North Point Light, Lowestoft Star, Lowestoft Star. Running before it from the north. Can't hold her head up. Advise, over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Lowestoft Star, North Point. Stand by. I've another boat on the East Gut. You're next. Over.

history.name: Lowestoft Star
history.speaker: LOWESTOFT
history.text: Don't be long, North Point.
Both in. Both in. The engine's knocking like a fist on a table.
Coming up on two o'clock. I know what this hour sounds like in this room.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: North Point Light, this is motor vessel Iona Star, Iona Star. Passage report, over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Iona Star, North Point. Go ahead, over.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: Glasgow for Stornoway, twelve souls aboard. We expect to pass abeam of your light at oh-five-hundred. Request local conditions, over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Severe gale nine, storm ten imminent. Seas very high off the Gut. Keep well out to the east until you're past. Over.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: Understood. Keep well east. Who am I speaking to, North Point? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Callum Mackay, principal keeper. Over.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: Mackay.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: My father's boat was lost under your light, Mr Mackay. Eighteen years ago tonight.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: This is Elspeth Ross. First mate. I wanted you to know who was out here.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: Someone sent me a letter last month. No name on it. "The light was out. Your father was not to blame."

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: I'd like to know who writes a letter like that and doesn't sign it. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I'm sorry, Miss Ross. I was there that night.

history.name: Elspeth Ross
history.speaker: ELSPETH
history.text: ...Were you. Then you'll keep your light burning tonight. Iona Star out.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: North Point, Stornoway. Callum, are you there? Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: I'm here.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: I've something I should have said a long time ago. I've got it in front of me. My notebook from that night. Pencil. I kept it in my handbag for eighteen years like a fool.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Mayday from Mary Ellen received at oh-one-fifty-two. And what he said was:

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: "No light at North Point. Repeat. No light"
Bang. The room goes black.
Lamps out. Radio dead. Above my head the motor winds down and stops.
Only the red lamp on the distribution cabinet, glowing like a coal. The main breaker.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: ...North Point! Callum! Answer me!

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Lost the main breaker. I'm back. Light's back. Over.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Thank God. Callum, did you hear what I said? Oh-one-fifty-two. No light. Your father's log says the light failed at oh-two-ten. After she struck.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Eighteen minutes, Callum. They hanged Alasdair Ross's name on eighteen minutes.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: You told me you were there. So tell me.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: The log says oh-two-ten. The log is right.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: ...Right.

history.name: Morag Fraser
history.speaker: MORAG
history.text: Right. I'll write that in my log, then. "North Point confirms the log." Stornoway out.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: North Point, Kittiwake. Callum, you'll think I'm daft. Over.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Go ahead, Rory.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: I'm tied up in the Sound, and I've been watching. There's a boat came out from the lee of Pabbay. Old wooden boat, a wee motor-fisher. No lights. Not a single light, Callum.

history.name: Rory Bain
history.speaker: RORY
history.text: She's heading your way. Not for the Sound. For your landing, under the light. Over.
On the radar a small hard echo is moving in from the north, steady as a clock.
There she is on the radar. Small, steady, coming down the North Sound like she's done it a thousand times.
No lights. In this. Nobody runs dark in this unless they want to.
If I put the beam on her by hand, I'll see what she is.
She slides into the lee of the island before I can put the light on her. But I saw the bow as she turned. S Y two one four.
SY 214 was the Mary Ellen.
She's alongside the landing below the light. The engine note drops, coughs, stops.
Then she's dark. Not a lantern. Not a cigarette.
[A dead carrier on Channel 16]
The speaker's gone quiet. Not static. A carrier, flat and steady, with nobody on it.
Somebody's sitting on sixteen.
[Footsteps on the jetty, slow]
Nobody comes up those stairs but the relief keeper and the engineer. Neither of them at half past two in the morning.
A hundred and nine steps. I've counted them every day for nine years.
[The base door, far below]
[A cough, deep in the chest. It goes on a long time.]
[Footsteps on the stair. One step at a time.]
[Silence]
[Three slow knocks]
Three knocks. Slow. Evenly spaced, like a man who has all night.

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: Evening, keeper.

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: I could not see your light.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: Who's there?

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: A man who's come a long way in poor weather. That's enough to be going on with.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: How do you know my name?

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: Your father's boy. You were thin as a boathook, and you used to sing to the clockwork when you wound it. Fear a' bhàta. Your father hated that song.

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: He kept a half-bottle of Grant's behind the Admiralty Tables. Top shelf. Is it still there?

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: The clockwork stuck tonight, didn't it. At forty-six degrees. It always did.
[He coughs. It goes on a long time.]

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: Open the door, Callum. I'm sixty-four, I'm soaked to the bone, and I've no wish to harm you. I want to talk to you before I die. I'll not be long about either.

history.name: Callum
history.speaker: CALLUM
history.text: (Keep the door shut.)

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: ...Aye. I'd have done the same, at your age, with a ghost at the door.
[Something slides under the door]
A photograph, cracked and soft as cloth.
Eight men on a deck at Leverburgh pier. The one at the wheel is laughing. On the back, in pencil: "Mary Ellen, July 1953. A. Ross, master."

history.name: The man at the door
history.speaker: VISITOR
history.text: I'll talk through the door, then. I've talked to worse.
